intervals.note: Start: underground assembly of the outer cryostat vessel (Dec 2018). End: DOE CD-4 project completion (21 Sep 2020).
intervals.quote: U.S. Department of Energy officials on Sept. 21 formally signed off on project completion for LUX-ZEPLIN, or LZ

intervals.label: commissioning
intervals.note: Bounds are approximate: commissioning was under way in October 2020 and ended when SR1 data taking began on 23 December 2021. No source gives exact commissioning start/end dates.
intervals.quote: We are completing commissioning of the detector – the testing phase – and will be looking at LZ data next year

intervals.label: science operations
intervals.locator: Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 041002 (2022 preprint), SR1 data-taking period
intervals.note: Open interval: LZ is still taking data (latest results presented September 2026).

name: LZ detector
notes: Energy threshold: not recorded. No official page or fetched paper states a single nuclear-recoil analysis threshold; the SR1 paper reports detection efficiency reaching 50% near 5.5 keV_nr, which is an efficiency point rather than a threshold. Left null.

The detector paper mentions "Twenty-two tonnes of GdLS contained in 150 55-gallon drums", which is the quantity procured/shipped rather than the outer detector mass, so no GdLS mass quantity is recorded.

placements.note: Start = week of the news item (17 December 2018) in which underground assembly of the Outer Cryostat Vessel (OCV) began in the Davis Cavern on the 4850 Level. The same page says four acrylic tanks were already lowered into the LZ water tank at the Davis Campus in November 2018, so earlier underground installation work existed; the start is therefore the beginning of OCV assembly, not of all underground work.
placements.quote: either at the Surface Assembly Laboratory (SAL) or in the Davis Cavern on the 4850 Level, researchers have begun the meticulous work of piecing together a 10-ton dark matter detector. ... Underground assembly of the OCV began this week. ... December 17, 2018

active_mass.note: Active liquid xenon mass in the TPC.
active_mass.quote: The LZ TPC monitors 7 active tonnes (5.6 tonnes fiducial) of LXe above its cathode.

depth.quote: in the same cavern as LZ (vertical depth of about 1480 m)

fiducial_mass.note: Fiducial mass of the SR1 WIMP search. The detector paper quotes a design fiducial of 5.6 t (NIM A 953, Sec. 1) — see conflicts in docs/atlas-worklog/dark-matter.md.
fiducial_mass.quote: using a fiducial mass of 5.5 t

phase.quote: a dual-phase xenon time projection chamber operating at the Sanford Underground Research Facility

pmt_count.note: TPC arrays only: 253 in the top array and 241 in the bottom array (NIM A 953, Sec. 2.1). The Xe skin and outer detector PMTs are extra.
pmt_count.quote: LZ utilizes 494 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) for signal detection

shielding.quote: Rejection of backgrounds is enhanced by a Xe skin veto detector and by a liquid scintillator Outer Detector loaded with gadolinium for efficient neutron capture and tagging.
shielding.value: Liquid xenon skin veto, a gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector, and an 8 m x 6 m tank of 70,000 gallons of ultrapure water, under ~1480 m of rock.

tank_diameter.note: Water shield tank. SURF's science director quotes 7.6 m diameter x 6.4 m high (arXiv:2403.13671) — see conflicts.
tank_diameter.quote: 8 meter diameter by 6 meter high water shield containing 70,000 gallons of purified water

tank_height.quote: 8 meter diameter by 6 meter high water shield containing 70,000 gallons of purified water

target_medium.quote: containing seven active tonnes of liquid xenon

total_mass.locator: arXiv:1910.09124 (NIM A 953 (2020) 163047), xenon handling / krypton-removal text
total_mass.note: Total xenon inventory of the experiment.
total_mass.quote: The entire 10 tonne Xe inventory is processed in 16 kg batches.

description.quote: A downward-looking "top" array located in the gas phase features 253 units
description.value: Dual-phase xenon TPC about 1.5 m in diameter and height with a 145.6 cm drift region, read out by 253 top and 241 bottom 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410 PMTs.

description.note: The 131 figure is the sum of the 93 1-inch, 20 2-inch bottom and 18 2-inch dome PMTs listed in Sec. 2.2; the paper does not print a single total.
description.quote: the Xe Skin detector contains an additional ∼2 tonnes of liquid
description.value: An instrumented layer of about 2 tonnes of liquid xenon outside the TPC field cage, read out by 131 1-inch and 2-inch PMTs, used to veto gamma rays that scatter in both volumes.

description.quote: A total of 120 Hamamatsu R5912 8–inch PMTs view the GdLS
description.value: Acrylic tanks of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator surrounding the cryostat, viewed by 120 Hamamatsu R5912 8-inch PMTs, tagging neutrons by capture on gadolinium.

description.quote: 8 meter diameter by 6 meter high water shield containing 70,000 gallons of purified water
description.value: A tank 8 m in diameter and 6 m high holding 70,000 gallons of purified water, which contains the outer detector and cryostat and suppresses gamma rays and neutrons from the cavern rock.

summary.plain: A tank of seven tonnes of cold liquid xenon, watched by hundreds of light sensors, that records the tiny flash and spark made if a dark matter particle bumps into a xenon atom. Layers of xenon, scintillator and water around it screen out ordinary radiation.
summary.technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC, ~1.5 m diameter and height, 145.6 cm drift, 7 active tonnes of a 10 t inventory, 5.5 t SR1 fiducial, 494 R11410 PMTs (253 top / 241 bottom), surrounded by a ~2 t instrumented Xe skin (131 PMTs), a gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector (120 R5912 PMTs) and an 8 m x 6 m water shield in the Davis Cavern.

technology.quote: a two-phase time projection chamber (TPC), containing seven active tonnes of liquid xenon
technology.value: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid xenon time projection chamber
